task: W72 layered source byte identity + pending saved-part ownership guard
scope: Private candidate only; no live canvas/controller files, native app, provider, server, or project data were changed.
changes: Layered imports with a valid sourceBytesSha256 commit file-sha256:<64 lowercase hex>; a present malformed digest throws before document commit.

Older backends missing sourceBytesSha256 retain a clearly weak composite-sha256:<digest> identity. On no-WebCrypto fallback, the identity is separately tagged composite-fnv1a32:<digest>, avoiding a false SHA-256 claim.

The durable part-memory runtime is gated at its actual isCommitted callback: layered imports qualify only with file-sha256 identity. This blocks durable capture/hydration for older backends while leaving normal source loading and scoped current-session helper code in place.

The edit queue prior-part check now counts sanitized unresolved pending provenance, so a source-color roof request cannot add a new source roof over an inert saved roof; an unrelated pending part remains unaffected.

verification.syntax: node --check passed for candidate canvas and pro-ai source.
verification.method: Executed extracted actual candidate fingerprint helper, the actual ensurePartMemoryRuntime isCommitted hook, actual editKey/pending-owner helper, and actual queueEditZones against controlled stubs. No full app cold load or native test.

limitations: The harness proves helper selection and callback/queue boundaries from actual candidate source, but it does not run a full browser/canvas source-load commit.

A valid backend digest must be supplied by the separately isolated W71 backend candidate before the strong path can activate; older servers continue to load with weak composite identity but cannot persist/rebind named-part ownership.
The W72 patch does not change persisted schema fields or add raw bytes; it relies on exact tagged fingerprint equality already present in the W53 memory binding.
